relevance_note: Single-centre cohort of 79 monogenic AID patients that includes two PSTPIP1 patients with individual variants: 'The genotypes were de novo mutations of p.E250K and p.N236K'.
method_note: Built by hand with a short script (no table transcription). Only the two PAID (PSTPIP1) patients are in scope; the other 77 diagnosed and 288 tested patients are out of scope. The paper gives no labels, so the two PSTPIP1 patients are 'unnamed person 1' (p.E250K) and 'unnamed person 2' (p.N236K), in order of mention of their variants; the paper lists one genotype per patient but never ties sex or age to a variant. Table 2 gives group-level sex 1:1 and onset median 2 (0-4) for n = 2; these were not assigned to individuals (sex and onset not reported). Features come from the named-group sentence 'Both patients had ...'; hepatosplenomegaly was mapped to both splenomegaly and hepatomegaly, pancytopenia to anemia, neutropenia and thrombocytopenia. Table 2's 'Fever, hematological problems, arthritis, rash' is a group summary without counts, so fever was left not reported. 'Persistent systemic inflammation' was recorded as a feature but not mapped to the elevated-inflammatory-markers checklist item; the cohort's elevated inflammation indices are an inclusion criterion and were not used. Inheritance is 'not reported' because the paper calls the variants de novo without describing parental testing (rule 8); the de novo statement is quoted in parental_testing_statement. Zygosity not stated (only 'AD' / 'dominantly inherited disease'). The functional statement (increased binding to pyrin) is cited from reference 23, not measured here. Ethnicity (Chinese) and no consanguinity come from cohort-wide statements covering all included children. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is true only because the NLRP12 patients (out of scope) were reported before in reference 12; nothing says the PSTPIP1 patients were previously published. No contradictions found.
